concept: The story is a set being completed, so the hero reads like a checklist: Australia, England and South Africa sit in muted grey and 'Now New Zealand.' lands in white as the final box ticked, with 4/4 underneath. Slide 2 shows why India are on top: two bars for the two century stands, each with a different partner but the same man at the other end. Slide 3 gives Rahul's role one giant number, 265 balls faced by tea, because his patience is what let Jaiswal and Padikkal score around him. The last slide sets the scene for the rest of the Test with the tea score and a question. Cricket blue, type and data only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
Australia. England. South Africa. Now New Zealand.

KL Rahul made an unbeaten 124 on day 3 in Wellington. That makes him the first Indian opener with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries. It was also his first Test innings in New Zealand: only Sunil Gavaskar and Surinder Amarnath had made a hundred in theirs before him.

Why India are on top: Rahul was in both of the first two stands. 130 with Yashasvi Jaiswal (85 off 89). Then 165 with Devdutt Padikkal (80) before Kyle Jamieson bowled Padikkal. India have had 100 stands for each of the first two wickets in a SENA Test only four times.

At tea India were 344 for 2 in reply to New Zealand's 368, with Rahul and Shubman Gill (36 not out off 40) together.
